notes.title: Thank you for your feedback!
notes.content:
Steam Next Fest is coming to an end. Thank you to everyone who has tried the technical demo of the game, provided feedback, or added the game to wishlist.

As this is my first game, all the feedback has been incredibly valuable and will help in creating a truly high-quality game.

The main issues that I have taken note of and will prioritize addressing are:

1. Fixing the head bobbing and overall player camera settings.
2. Improving the locomotion system, including the idle state and running.
3. Adding more interactivity to the demo. In reality, there are many mechanics in the game, but they are either incomplete or not functioning correctly. I didn't have enough time to complete everything before the start of the festival.
4. Working on the controls (specifically finishing the gamepad support).
5. Enhancing the points of interest.
Additionally, I will continue to learn Unreal Engine, Blender, and Substance Painter.

Don't forget to follow us on social media to stay updated on the game's development progress.

notes.title: 60 days until the release of Out of the Woods demo version. Development status
notes.content:
Hello! The main work on the inventory system is complete, which means the necessary minimum for the release of the Out of the Woods demo version is done! However, there is still a lot of work to be done on points of interest, user interface (main menu, inventory appearance, etc.), as well as the health and stamina system. The latter is not so obvious and simple: the demo version will feature a greatly simplified system (most likely, I won't have time to implement what I planned for the summer Steam Next Fest).

In the release version of Out of the Woods, there will be a more complex system based on the real capabilities of the human body. So the "rule of three" will apply:

[list] [*] 3 minutes without air on average before a person loses consciousness
[/list] [list]
[*] 3 days without water, after which dehydration occurs, which is dangerous to life
[/list] [list]
[*] 3 weeks without food without serious harm to health.
[/list]
Of course, a long absence of water or food will affect the speed of movement, the ability to carry more items, and other things.

I hope to implement everything I planned within 30-45 days, and then I will start testing and fixing bugs (I think 10-14 days will be enough for this)

notes.title: Current state of the game
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
This is the first post about the game on Steam. There is no time for PR at the moment, so there is not much news about the game on social networks. But since I receive questions and suggestions by email, I decided to tell you a little about the state of the game and the upcoming plans.

[h2][u][b]To begin with, a little information for publishers and those who want to help with development[/b][/u][/h2]

1. The only and official email - [b]oleg-yankovsky@wi1dd0g-games.ru[/b] . You should not send emails to other mail addresses
2. I am currently working on a demo version of the game, a full-fledged PR will begin after its release.
3. I'm sorry I don't reply to emails, but I send them to a special folder so they won't get lost. At the right moment, I will contact those who are suitable.

[h2][u][b]End of information for Publishers[/b][/u][/h2]


[b][h1]Game development[/h1][/b]
At the moment, the demo version includes a map (approximately 2 x 2 kilometers in size), the most basic mechanics and a prototype of the main menu.
We are actively working on lighting, creating a system for changing the time of day and weather. After that, inventory and some items will be created. Thus the game will go into beta test. 

I am also now carefully considering whether it is worth transferring the game from Unreal Engine 4 to Unreal Engine 5. I have not found any obstacles so far, except for the requirements of the engine itself to the resources of the computer. But the picture looks livelier and juicier, just look! The first screenshot is UE4, and the second is UE5:
